title: Unify quantized-kernel loader + adaptive ABI fallback for heterogeneous GPU stacks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We currently ship multiple incompatible kernel loading paths for quantized kernels (int8/int4) across CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS versions. This causes runtime OOMs and symbol lookup failures on mixed fleet hosts and complicates model rollout.

Goal: Implement a single adaptive kernel loader that probes available CUTLASS/Triton symbols at startup, prefers optimized kernels when ABI matches, and gracefully falls back to safe generic kernels when minor symbol/version mismatches are detected. The loader must support: (1) multi-cutlass version discovery, (2) quantization-specific kernel selection (per-model profile), (3) an opt-in runtime flag for strict-ABI mode for Dedicated customers, and (4) CI gating with simulated older driver / older CUTLASS combinations.

Why now: We've seen a 12% increase in kernel selection incidents in the error-rate dashboard after the CUDA 13 pilot. This refactor will reduce operational incidents, simplify model onboarding, and unlock safer auto-quantization rollouts.
tasks: Design adaptive loader API and config (PRD link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/r/runtime-adaptive-loader)
Implement symbol-probe module that checks for CUTLASS symbol table + Triton plugin presence
Add per-model kernel preference override in model manifest parsing
Introduce 'strict_abi' runtime flag (defaults to false for hosted, true for Dedicated optional)
Write kernel compatibility unit tests (mocked driver + libcutlass stubs)
Extend nightly CI matrix to include old-driver (cuda11.8) and new-driver (cuda13.0) permutations
Create migration plan and deprecation notice for legacy loader
Prepare release notes and runtime rollout runbook
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive loader selects optimized CUTLASS kernels when symbols match and falls back to generic kernels without crashing
No increase in median latency for typical generation workloads (<= 2% regression in staging)
Nightly CI shows green across at least 4 driver + CUTLASS permutations
Dedicated clusters can enable 'strict_abi' and fail fast on symbol mismatches
Automated canary rollout for models using new loader with rollback on increased error-rate

rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag 'adaptive_kernel_loader' and enable in staging
Deploy to 10% of hosted runtime nodes for 48h, monitor kernel fallback metric and latency
If stable, expand to 50% and run full test harness (regression prompts + perf)
Offer Dedicated customers a toggle 'strict_abi' and coordinate with accounts for early opt-in
Complete full rollout and deprecate legacy loader after 8 weeks with customer communications
risk_mitigation: Keep legacy loader as fallback and provide fast rollback path (single toggled switch)
Add telemetry tags on each kernel selection decision to triage model-specific regressions
Limit optimized-kernel selection to models with explicit opt-in or black-boxed evals to avoid silent quality regressions
Run long-running generation workloads in canary to catch subtle numerical regressions from kernel variant changes
